## H1: Error-Mask Boolean Algebra as Lattice of Independent Constraints
The Boolean algebra B_n (error masks under OR) is isomorphic to the lattice of independent constraint subsets in a factorized system. The partition function factorizes into a product over lattice atoms.

Prediction: Z_global = product of Z_local. |distinct masks| = 2^n.

## H2: Sediment Layers as Extreme Points of Convex Constraint Spaces
Accumulated correctness = iteratively adding edge-case constraints that are extreme points of convex feasible set. Space remains convex after each addition.

Prediction: Volume decreases monotonically, set stays convex, layers = facets of final polytope.

Intelligence of a procedure is a tiling of the error mask Boolean algebra. IEEE 754 monotonicity ensures exact tiling boundaries (no overlap/gaps).

Prediction: IEEE 754 = zero ambiguous selections. Non-monotonic = nonzero ambiguity rate.

Accumulated correctness is a sheaf cohomology process. Each edge case is a local section. Gluing is enforced by the procedure. IEEE 754 = exact local comparison.

## H6: Error Masks as Subgradients of the Partition Function
Error mask Boolean algebra is DUAL to partition function factorization. Subgradient of log Z w.r.t. constraint strength gives the violation probability (= error mask bit).

Prediction: ∂log Z/∂w_i = P(violation_i) exactly. This gives a thermodynamic interpretation of the error mask.

Adding sediment layers to a constraint system produces a monotonically non-decreasing correctness sequence that converges to 1.0. This is the formalization of why COBOL systems work.

Prediction: Correctness follows a power law (rapid early gains, slow refinement). Converges to 1.0 in finite steps for finite input spaces.

A procedure tile (discovery 5) can be compressed using the thermodynamic distribution of its error masks (discovery 2). High-probability error patterns get short codes. This is Huffman coding on the partition function.
